subject: humanities
passage: The cave temple at Dambulla, in central Sri Lanka, occupies five chambers hollowed beneath an overhanging granite ridge. According to tradition, a king who had been driven from his throne in the first century BCE sheltered in the caves and, after regaining power, had them turned into a shrine. The roughly 150 statues that the caves ______ images of the Buddha seated, standing, and reclining; figures of two Sri Lankan kings; and several Hindu gods. Most of the murals visible today were repainted in the eighteenth century, when the kingdom of Kandy sponsored a wave of restoration.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the third sentence is "The roughly 150 statues that the caves hold," and its verb is "include." The verb leads directly into the list that is its object. No punctuation may separate a subject from its verb or a verb from its object, even when the object is a long list.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon must be followed by an independent clause, and it cannot separate the verb "include" from the list that is its object.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The comma separates the subject "The roughly 150 statues that the caves hold" from its verb "include."
explanation.C: Incorrect. A colon may introduce a list only after a complete clause; "The roughly 150 statues that the caves hold include" is not complete until its object follows, so the colon separates the verb from its object.
explanation.D: Correct. The subject, the verb "include," and the list that is its object follow one another with no punctuation between them.
